summary: AI-Native Operational Autonomy - Cognitive Reasoning Layer successfully implemented
objective: Develop the cognitive reasoning layer to generate explainable policy decisions using telemetry, predictive signals, and RL outputs without performing direct actions

files_created.description: Structured reasoning output format with comprehensive data structures for explainable decisions
Cognitive policy reasoner that synthesizes RL, predictive, and telemetry signals into explainable recommendations
Module definition and public API for cognitive control layer
Comprehensive shadow evaluation tests covering 10 scenarios

reasoning_capabilities.description: Combines Phase 11.1 RL agent outputs, Phase 11.2 predictive forecasts, and current telemetry into unified reasoning
Generates human-readable rationale explaining primary reasons, supporting evidence, key observations, trade-offs, and preference justification
Quantifies rollback risk, performance degradation risk, disruption risk with identified risk factors and mitigation strategies
Computes overall confidence (0.0-1.0) based on RL agent confidence, risk assessment, and signal quality
Recommends policy actions (increase/decrease batch, adjust routing, rollback, no-action) with target parameters and expected impact
Documents alternative actions considered with rejection reasons and confidence scores
Identifies anomalies in telemetry (high error rate, high latency, resource pressure)
Analyzes historical telemetry trends (increasing/decreasing/stable) for latency, throughput, errors
All reasoning artifacts are proposals only - no execution, no orchestrator state mutations
Reasoning outputs serialized to JSON format for easy analysis and integration
